questions.question: Which feature is part of a mineral's introductory geological definition?
choices: Formation only by human manufacturing
A required metallic appearance
An ordered crystal structure
A composition consisting of several visible rocks

questions.question: What does mineral hardness measure?
choices: Resistance to breaking in any way
Resistance to scratching
Mass per unit volume
Brightness in sunlight

questions.question: What is a mineral's streak?
choices: The color of its largest crystal
The direction of its magnetic field
The size of its grains
The color of its powder

questions.question: What does luster describe?
choices: Its resistance to scratching
Its electrical charge
Its melting temperature
How a mineral's surface reflects light

questions.question: What is cleavage?
choices: Breaking only into curved irregular surfaces
Breaking along preferred planes of weakness
Changing into another element
Dissolving completely in every liquid

questions.question: What is fracture in mineral identification?
choices: The growth of a perfect crystal
A mineral's powder color
Breakage that does not follow cleavage planes
Its reaction with oxygen only

questions.question: What is the hardest reference mineral on the Mohs scale?
choices: Diamond
Talc
Calcite
Gypsum

questions.question: Why is color alone often unreliable for mineral identification?
choices: Every mineral has the same color
Impurities can change a mineral's color
Color determines atomic number directly
A mineral's color never varies

questions.question: Why should several mineral properties be tested together?
choices: Different minerals may share one property but differ in others
One color identifies every mineral conclusively
Hardness and streak always have identical values
All tests measure the same characteristic

questions.question: Why can streak be useful when surface colors vary?
choices: Powder has no chemical composition
Grinding creates a new element
Powder color can be more consistent than surface color
Streak always equals the crystal's shape

questions.question: How does crystal structure influence cleavage?
choices: Only overall crystal size controls cleavage
Cleavage removes all atoms from the surface
Every mineral must cleave into cubes
Weak bonding directions can favor particular breakage planes

questions.question: What does the Mohs scale provide?
choices: Equal numerical steps in absolute hardness
A relative ranking of scratch resistance
A ranking of all mineral masses
A count of a mineral's electrons

questions.question: How do rocks and minerals relate?
choices: Every mineral consists of several rock types
Every rock is one chemical element
Minerals occur only inside sedimentary rocks
A rock can consist of one or more minerals

questions.question: Why can mineral density aid identification?
choices: Different compositions and structures can produce different mass-to-volume ratios
Every mineral has the same density
Density identifies color without measurement
Larger samples necessarily have greater density

questions.question: Why should a student avoid testing an unknown mineral by tasting it?
choices: Taste is required to measure hardness
Every mineral is edible but tasteless
It may be hazardous, and safer identification methods are available
Tasting determines crystal structure precisely

questions.question: A specimen scratches gypsum but is scratched by calcite. Gypsum has Mohs hardness 2 and calcite 3. What is supported?
choices: Its hardness is 1
Its hardness exceeds 10
Its hardness lies between about 2 and 3
Its density must be 2.5 g/cm³

questions.question: A mineral breaks repeatedly into flat surfaces at similar angles. Which property is being observed?
choices: Cleavage
Streak
Luster
Magnetism

questions.question: A dark specimen leaves a reddish-brown powder on a streak plate. Which observation records its streak?
choices: Dark surface color
The plate's width
The specimen's total mass
Reddish-brown

questions.question: A mineral has mass 30 g and volume 10 cm³. What is its density?
choices: 300 g/cm³
3 g/cm³
0.33 g/cm³
20 g/cm³

questions.question: Two yellow minerals look alike, but one scratches glass and the other does not under comparable tests. What does this suggest?
choices: Their hardness differs, so appearance alone is insufficient
They must be the same mineral
Both must have identical crystal structure
The glass test determines only their color
